facts: Japanese people bow (お辞儀) at different angles depending on formality.
"皆さん" (minasan) means "everyone" and is great for openings.
In Japan, nodding "はい" while listening doesn't always mean agreement.
Keigo (敬語), honorific language, is key to polite business communication.
The particle "は" is read "wa" as a topic marker, not "ha".
